label: Jennifer Hart Weed, Religious Language §2a: Church 1949: given three observation-statements O1…
locator: §2a, "we may show of any statement S whatever that either it or its negation is verifiable"
interpretation: Church's review of the second edition (JSL 14, 1949, p. 53), quoted verbatim by the IEP entry. The steps are: the auxiliary is directly verifiable because with O1 it entails O3; S with it entails O2; so S is indirectly verifiable unless the auxiliary alone entails O2, in which case not-S with O3 entails O2 and not-S is directly verifiable. Attribution reading on a secondary witness.
attribution: The passage states in a verbatim quotation of Church 1949, p. 53, that for three observation-statements none of which alone entails another, any statement S or its negation is verifiable under Ayer's definition through the statement (not-O1 and O2) or (O3 and not-S), which is the premise.
